```python
import itertools

# Propositions over possible worlds (exhaustive over all 2^4 truth assignments).
# N1: the stayers at home-less holidays are impoverished (the plan's target premise)
# N2: students are competent to do campus security work (the plan's means premise)
# N3: the security office's funds cover work-study for all stayers (feasibility premise)
# T:  most stayers have signed up for paid winter English tuition (unrelated to N1-N3)
#
# The plan achieves its aims only if N1, N2 and N3 all hold.
# An option questions the plan if its claim entails that the plan fails,
# i.e. in every world where the claim is true, at least one premise fails.

VARS = ["N1", "N2", "N3", "T"]
worlds = [dict(zip(VARS, bits)) for bits in itertools.product([False, True], repeat=len(VARS))]

def plan_ok(w):
    return w["N1"] and w["N2"] and w["N3"]

options = {
    # A: not all stayers are in financial difficulty -> target premise fails
    "A": lambda w: not w["N1"],
    # B: students are hardly competent for security work -> means premise fails
    "B": lambda w: not w["N2"],
    # C: funds are limited and stayers are numerous -> feasibility premise fails
    "C": lambda w: not w["N3"],
    # D: most stayers enrolled in paid English tuition -> no link to N1-N3
    "D": lambda w: w["T"],
}

results = {}
for label, claim in options.items():
    true_worlds = [w for w in worlds if claim(w)]
    # Entailment check: claim true => plan fails, in every world where claim holds
    entails_failure = all(not plan_ok(w) for w in true_worlds)
    # Witness: a world where the claim holds and the plan still succeeds
    witness = next((w for w in true_worlds if plan_ok(w)), None)
    results[label] = (entails_failure, witness)
    print(f"Option {label}: claim-true worlds = {len(true_worlds)} of {len(worlds)}; "
          f"entails plan failure = {entails_failure}; "
          f"non-questioning witness exists = {witness is not None}")

non_questioners = [k for k, (ent, _) in results.items() if not ent]
print("Options that cannot question the plan:", non_questioners)

submitted = "D"
if non_questioners == [submitted]:
    print("CHECK PASS: submitted answer D is the only option that cannot question the plan")
else:
    print("CHECK FAIL: submitted answer D does not match the computed non-questioner(s)")

print("Note: this is an exhaustive finite model of the stated premises. The mapping of each "
      "option onto N1-N3/T is an interpretation of the Chinese text, so the result is "
      "conditional on that mapping.")
```
